title: Maths reference: Angles and shapes
summary: The words and methods from Angles and shapes, each with an example and, where it helps, a picture of the board.
_about: Maths cards for maths/angles (see snippets/maths.json for the format).

items.label: transversal
items.hint: Parallel lines go the same way and never meet; arrows (>>) mark them. A transversal crosses both, making eight angles.

items.label: corresponding angles
items.hint: The same place at each crossing (an F shape). With parallel lines they are equal.
items.board:
widget: parallel
t: 60
pair: a, e
items.shows: a and e: the same place at each crossing, both 120°

items.label: alternate angles
items.hint: Between the parallel lines, on opposite sides of the transversal (a Z shape). With parallel lines they are equal.
items.board:
widget: parallel
t: 60
pair: c, f
items.shows: c and f: between the lines, opposite sides, both 60°

items.label: co-interior angles
items.hint: Between the parallel lines, on the same side (a C shape). With parallel lines they add to $180^\circ$: they are not equal unless both are $90^\circ$.
items.board:
widget: parallel
t: 60
pair: c, e
items.shows: c and e: between the lines, same side, 60° + 120° = 180°

items.label: vertically opposite angles
items.hint: Opposite each other at one crossing: always equal, parallel lines or not. Not one of the parallel-line pairs.

items.label: give a reason
items.hint: For each angle you find, name the rule: corresponding or alternate angles are equal; co-interior angles add to $180^\circ$; angles on a straight line add to $180^\circ$.

items.label: interior angle
items.hint: An angle inside a shape, at one of its corners.

items.label: polygon
items.hint: A closed shape with straight sides: triangle (3), quadrilateral (4), pentagon (5), hexagon (6), octagon (8).

items.label: regular polygon
items.hint: All sides and all angles are equal, so each angle is the angle sum shared equally: a regular hexagon has angles of $120^\circ$.

items.label: angle sum of a triangle
items.hint: True for every triangle, whatever its shape or size: tear off the corners and they fill a straight line.

items.label: angle sum of a polygon
items.hint: Split it into triangles from one corner: a shape with $n$ sides makes $n - 2$ triangles. A pentagon: $3 \times 180^\circ = 540^\circ$.
items.board:
widget: geometry
shape: polygon
sides: 5
corners: 2,1; 9,1; 10,5; 6,7; 1,5
split: shown
items.shows: A pentagon splits into 3 triangles from A: 540°

items.label: triangles by sides and angles
items.hint: Give two names: one for the sides (how many are equal) and one for the biggest angle. Equal sides sit opposite equal angles.
items.board:
widget: geometry
shape: triangle
corners: 2,1; 8,1; 5,5
classify: on
sum: off
items.shows: An isosceles acute triangle, its equal sides ticked

items.label: quadrilateral family
items.code: \text{every square is a rectangle; every rectangle is a parallelogram}
items.hint: Trapezium: at least one pair of parallel sides. Parallelogram: two. Rhombus: four equal sides. Rectangle: four right angles. Square: both. Kite: two pairs of equal neighbouring sides. A square is also a rectangle and a rhombus.
items.board:
widget: geometry
shape: polygon
sides: 4
corners: 3,1; 7,1; 7,5; 3,5
classify: on
sum: off
items.shows: A square with equal sides, parallel sides and right angles marked

items.label: regular polygon
items.hint: Both are needed: a rhombus has equal sides but is not regular. Names: pentagon 5, hexagon 6, heptagon 7, octagon 8, nonagon 9, decagon 10.

items.label: convex and concave
items.hint: Convex: every corner points out. Concave: at least one corner points in.
items.board:
widget: geometry
shape: polygon
sides: 6
corners: 2,1; 7,1; 9,4; 6,3; 4,6; 1,4
classify: on
sum: off
items.shows: A concave hexagon with one corner pointing in

items.label: net
items.hint: A net is a solid unfolded flat. Fold it, or roll a cube over it, to check that every face is covered once. Six squares is not enough.
items.shows: A cross of six squares that folds into a cube

items.label: prism net area
items.hint: A triangular prism has two triangles and three rectangles. The net's area is the surface area.

items.label: top, front and side views
items.hint: A view shows what you can see from one side; hidden cubes do not show. The top view with heights shows every cube.
items.shows: Three drawings of the same cubes

items.label: translation
items.hint: Every point slides the same way. Right and up add; left and down take away.
items.board:
widget: transform
mode: translate
shape: 1,1; 3,1; 3,2
range: 8
dx: 3
dy: -2
items.shows: A triangle moved 3 right and 2 down

items.label: reflection
items.hint: Each point and its image are the same distance from the mirror, on opposite sides.
items.board:
widget: transform
mode: reflect
shape: 2,1; 4,1; 4,3
range: 6
axis: y
items.shows: A triangle reflected in the y-axis

items.label: rotation
items.hint: Give the centre, the angle and the direction. A half turn: (x, y) to (−x, −y). 90° clockwise is 270° anticlockwise.
items.board:
widget: transform
mode: rotate
shape: 2,1; 4,1; 4,2
range: 6
t: 90
items.shows: A triangle turned a quarter turn about the origin

items.label: algorithm
items.hint: A set of steps and decisions that gives the right result every time. Test it on one shape of every class.

items.label: congruence tests
items.hint: Each set of equal parts fixes a triangle. In SAS the angle is between the two sides; SSA is not a test, because it can give two triangles.
items.board:
widget: congruence
test: SSA
p: 8
q: 6
s: 40
items.shows: Two different triangles with the same SSA parts

items.label: scale factor
items.hint: Similar shapes: every length times k, every angle the same. Triangles are similar by AA, SSS (sides in one ratio) or SAS.
items.board:
widget: similar
shape: triangle
sides: 3, 4, 5
k: 2
items.shows: A 3, 4, 5 triangle and a copy twice as big

items.label: diagonals of quadrilaterals
items.hint: A parallelogram's diagonals cut each other in half; a kite's cross at 90°. Prove a property with two congruent triangles.
items.board:
widget: geometry
shape: polygon
sides: 4
corners: 3,1; 9,1; 9,5; 3,5
classify: on
diagonals: on
sum: off
items.shows: A rectangle with its two equal diagonals

items.label: parallelogram angles
items.hint: Neighbouring angles are co-interior between parallel sides. All four add to 360°.

items.label: 3D coordinates
items.hint: Along x, along y, then up z. The order is always x, y, z; points on the floor have z = 0.

items.label: congruence algorithm
items.hint: Ask the congruence tests first, then the similarity conditions, and end with a catch-all. Test on one pair of each kind, including SSA.
